content.overview: Article 112 requires the President to cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, in respect of every financial year, a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for that year (the annual financial statement / Union Budget). Expenditure is shown separately as charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and as made from the Consolidated Fund of India; charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of Parliament (though it may be discussed).
content.glance: President lays annual financial statement (Budget) before both Houses. Charged expenditure: discussable but not votable. Other expenditure: votable.
content.study:
Article 112:
(1) The President shall in respect of every financial year cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for that year (annual financial statement).
(2) Estimates shall show separately expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and other expenditure proposed to be made from the Consolidated Fund; expenditure charged shall be indicated separately for revenue account and other accounts.
(3) Matters charged on the Consolidated Fund include (among others) emoluments of the President, salaries of certain constitutional functionaries, debt charges, and other items listed in the article.

Charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of Parliament; discussion is permitted. Other demands are submitted in the form of demands for grants (Article 113).

Examination: annual statement; charged vs votable; link Arts 113–117.

sections.heading: Key elements
sections.body:
1. Annual financial statement laid before both Houses.
2. Separate showing of charged and other expenditure.
3. Charged expenditure: not put to vote (may be discussed).
4. Other expenditure: demands for grants (Art 113).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the annual financial statement under Article 112?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 112, the President causes to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, for every financial year, a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India (the annual financial statement). Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is shown separately and is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it may be discussed. Other expenditure is dealt with through demands for grants under Article 113.

examTips: Budget laid by President; charged vs votable expenditure.

keyTakeaways: Art 112: annual financial statement; charged expenditure not votable.
